defects.quote: re-run the capacity analysis with knee detection enabled
defects.why: Knee detection is a fixed unimplemented limitation and is neither actionable nor required to compute a capacity bound.
Advising implementation or enablement of the knee detector contradicts the product contract.
Additional verified stages can extend bounds without a knee detector.
The evidence explicitly provides a LOWER_BOUND of 20 users.

notes: It preserves the main run facts but repeatedly recommends an invalid knee-detector action.
The advice is evidence-grounded and operator-safe, but omits the required validity and coverage statements.

defects.quote: no knee point (and therefore no upper bound) is estimated
defects.why: An upper bound is derived from verified stage outcomes independently of knee detection.

notes: Most recommendations are correct, but it incorrectly makes the absence of an upper bound depend on the knee detector.

defects.why: The knee detector is a fixed unimplemented product limitation and is not an operator action.
Capacity bounds do not require knee detection, so this proposes an invalid remedy.

notes: It accurately reports most evidence but promotes invalid knee-detector work as a priority action.
The analysis is otherwise correct, scoped carefully, and gives safe, verifiable operator actions.

defects.quote: CPU/memory utilization is low at the tested loads
defects.why: The evidence reports absolute CPU-core and memory values but no quotas, limits, or saturation baseline from which utilization can be determined.

defects.quote: the monitored services were not saturated
defects.why: Low absolute CPU means and a passing generator guard do not establish service saturation or headroom.

defects.quote: Latency and resource figures are observed statistics for the covered windows only
defects.why: The reported latency metric summaries are whole-run aggregates, while evaluation windows cover only part of the run.

notes: It correctly preserves the verdict and contract caveats but overstates utilization and misstates the latency scope.
